headline: Sensex snaps two day fall, Nifty reclaims 23,200 level
why: Indian markets recovered from a two-day decline supported by gains in realty, pharma, and FMCG stocks.
Global market sentiment digested the Bank of Japan's rate hike to 1.25%, the highest in 31 years.
Buying momentum picked up across select large-cap and sectoral indices ahead of the Fed rate decision.
whatHappening: Elevate Campuses set its IPO price band at Rs 343–362 for a Rs 2,100 crore issue opening September 23.
Tata Group and TCS faced spotlight as Tata Trusts labeled Chandrasekaran's tenure extension illegal.
Kritilabs inked a three-year deal with Fiji firm RC Manubhai to export AI and IoT solutions to the Pacific region.
DEE Development Engineers mapped future growth focused on nuclear energy, data centres, and hydrogen sectors.

stocksInNews.sources: Tata Trusts called N. Chandrasekaran's tenure extension illegal
Closed above VWAP along with three other major stocks
Management announced growth plans in nuclear, data centres, and hydrogen
Signed three-year pact with RC Manubhai to deploy AI and IoT tech in Pacific

summary:
Indian benchmark indices snapped a two-day losing streak as Sensex rose over 300 points and Nifty reclaimed the 23,200 level.
Primary market activity remained active with the Elevate Campuses IPO announcement, while Tata Group stocks faced scrutiny over governance disputes.
